tier_reason: Independent third-party CI shootout (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, v8-v7 suite forked from mozilla/arewefastyet, run daily by .github/workflows/update.yml on macos-latest, ubuntu-latest and windows-latest) lists lumen 0.1.3.f6c9860 at Score 3953 vs QuickJS 2026.06.04 at 1761 on macos-arm64 in the 10/5/2026 snapshot; code is public but the runners' CPU models and the engines' compiler flags are not stated, so not A (same B precedent as ChakraCore, ant, njs, quanta in this wave).

corrections.claimed_speedup: ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark macos-arm64 table (run dated 10/5/2026): lumen Score 3953 vs QuickJS 1761, quickjs-ng 1660, hermes 1233, i.e. 2.24x QuickJS (derived from page data). The composite win comes from three numeric subtests: Richards 11374 vs 1246, Crypto 10633 vs 1170, NavierStokes 21200 vs 2349 (about 9x each, derived from page data); lumen is slower than QuickJS on RayTrace (1925 vs 2408), EarleyBoyer (1808 vs 3217) and Splay (5444 vs 5786). Same table: JavaScriptCore 67664, v8 64220, bun 46772, node 37405, so lumen is about 16x below V8 (derived from page data). Ubuntu table: lumen 444 vs QuickJS 1217 (0.36x, slower on all eight subtests), v8 48107. No Windows result for lumen.
corrections.caveats: The README makes no speed claim; the claim here comes only from a third-party engine shootout. The advantage over QuickJS appears on the macOS arm64 runner only, and only in the composite: lumen wins Richards, Crypto, NavierStokes, DeltaBlue and RegExp but loses RayTrace, EarleyBoyer and Splay to QuickJS there. On the Ubuntu x86-64 runner lumen scores 444 against QuickJS 1217 and is slower on every subtest; the README says the full set of inline JIT fast paths lives only in the ARM64 backend, while the x86-64 backend is correctness-first with checked per-op helpers. Lumen is not run on Windows in the shootout. It is far behind JIT engines (V8, JavaScriptCore, Node, Bun) on both platforms. Lumen's own docs/closure-numeric-regions.md says Djot takes about 15.5x Node's time and 23.9x Bun's, and docs/closure-call-cache.md says the 'within-2x Node/Bun objective remains unmet'. The shootout's lumen version column reads 0.1.3.f6c9860 and the GitHub Actions CPU model is not recorded.

notes: Every number in the record matches the ahaoboy README tables (10/5/2026 snapshot); metadata checked (MIT, 271 stars, 8 forks, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-24, JS backend of lucid-softworks/browser). Shortcomings to record: win over QuickJS is arm64-only and driven by three numeric subtests (loses RayTrace, EarleyBoyer, Splay), slower than QuickJS on x86-64 Ubuntu on all subtests, no Windows run, far below V8/JSC/Node/Bun, own docs say about 15.5x Node's time on Djot.

corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the numbers come from a WebSearch snippet that quotes porffor.dev; the site is blocked by egress policy so hardware, versions, flags and date could not be read, hence tier C at most. The QuickJS, Node --jitless and Bun no-JIT figures are first-party runs of unknown versions on unknown hardware. The committed repo README has no numbers (only 'compiled hello.js in 105ms, 33.7KB') and now describes Porffor as compiling JS to C through an IR, with no Wasm mention; the README no longer says pre-alpha. Porffor is far slower than JIT-enabled V8 and JavaScriptCore on the same suite (Node and Bun with JIT score 13 to 17x higher), so the win is over Node's interpreter-only mode and QuickJS. Porffor is not in the ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark shootout. Third-party harness jlucaso1/js-compiled (also proggeramlug/js-compiled) benchmarks Porffor vs Node, Bun and scriptc on 22 programs, but its results are published only on GitHub Pages (blocked) and are not committed (no results/ or REPORT.md in the tree, no gh-pages branch). The bench/ directory has 25 benchmark programs plus an ffi/ subdirectory (richards.js, v8-v7.js and more) but no results file.

tier_reason: The startup figures (scriptc 0.0.16 median CLI startup 1.78 ms vs Bun 1.3.12 21.29 ms vs Node 24.18.0 61.78 ms; 1.9 MiB idle node:http server) appear only in WebSearch snippets of launch coverage (InfoQ, EGRESS_BLOCKED here); who ran them, on what hardware and with which program could not be read, and the repo has no Node or Bun comparison, so C (snippet-only precedent).

corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the startup numbers come from WebSearch result snippets of news coverage (InfoQ and other outlets, all blocked here); the original run's author, hardware and measured program could not be identified (one search summary attributes it to Vercel Labs' launch, which would make it vendor evidence), and the figures were measured on scriptc 0.0.16 while the current release is 0.2.4. Neither the scriptc README, the docs/ site source, nor CHANGELOG.md contains a Node or Bun comparison; benchmarks/builds and scripts/bench-builds.mjs measure build latency, not Node or Bun. Throughput is the weak side: issue #357 (closed, opened 2026-09-20) measured xorshift32 at 88.878 ms/op vs Node 24.12.0 1.148 ms/op (77.4x slower) and a byte loop 56.4x slower, and its fix brought xorshift to 1.174 ms/op (about 1.02x Node); issue #113 (closed, opened 2026-08-10) measured scriptc 0.0.23 byte loops 2.1x to 6.5x slower than Node 22. A search snippet also quotes one Hacker News commenter measuring about 7.5x slower than Node 24 on byte arrays, while startup was 12x faster (1.5 ms vs 18.6 ms) and memory 72x lower (2.5 MiB vs 181 MiB). Hono needs --dynamic (embedded quickjs-ng) and then reaches 18.4k requests per second vs 70.5k for Bun. Third-party harnesses (proggeramlug/js-compiled and jlucaso1/js-compiled) benchmark scriptc against Node, Bun and Porffor on 22 programs, but results are only on GitHub Pages (blocked) and not committed. The startup advantage is structural for an AOT native executable versus a full JS runtime.

Shortcomings to record: startup-only win from snippet numbers of unknown provenance on an old version (0.0.16 vs current 0.2.4), sustained throughput slower than Node (issues #357, #113, HN 7.5x report), Hono via --dynamic 3.8x below Bun.
